traceability.evidence:
1) Story file verification - Read docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md and confirmed it matches exactly the specification provided in the prompt, including Acceptance Criteria, Requirements (REQ-TEST-FIX-*), Implementation Notes (template shape, malformed prefix rules, safety constraints), configuration options, and Definition of Done checklist.
2) Implementation – ESLint rule and helpers - File: src/rules/require-test-traceability.ts - Contains the ESLint rule implementing test traceability validation and auto-fix. - `meta.fixable` is set to `"code"`, enabling ESLint `--fix` behavior. - Rule options type includes: - `autoFixTestTemplate?: boolean;` - `autoFixTestPrefixFormat?: boolean;` - `testSupportsTemplate?: string;` - `meta.schema` defines these options with defaults matching the story (autoFix flags default true, optional template string). - In `create(context)`, options are destructured with defaults and passed into helper functions: - `ensureFileSupportsAnnotation(context, sourceCode, { autoFixTestTemplate, testSupportsTemplate })` – controls file-level `@supports` template insertion. - `handleCallExpression` is invoked for `CallExpression` nodes with options including `autoFixTestPrefixFormat`, so malformed `[REQ-...]` prefixes can be normalized when enabled. - JSDoc on the rule includes: - `@supports docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE`, directly mapping the rule to this story and its requirements.
- File: src/rules/helpers/require-test-traceability-helpers.ts - `buildSupportsTemplateComment(customTemplate?)`: - Uses the default base template `"@supports docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ"` when no custom template is provided. - Produces a multi-line JSDoc block: ``` /** * @supports docs/stories/XXX.X-STORY-NAME.story.md REQ-XXX-YYY REQ-XXX-ZZZ * TODO: Replace the placeholder story path and REQ-IDs with real values for this test file. */ ``` - This matches the story’s template example and satisfies template quality and placeholder clarity (REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE, REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER). - `insertSupportsTemplate(fixer, sourceCode, customTemplate?)`: - Detects a shebang (`#!`) and inserts the template after it; otherwise inserts at the start of the file. - Uses `fixer.insertTextBeforeRange([insertIndex, insertIndex], templateComment)`, only adding a comment and not modifying code, preserving test semantics (REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE). - `ensureFileSupportsAnnotation(context, sourceCode, autoFixOptions)`: - Scans all comments for `@supports`; if present, does nothing (no duplicate templates). - If missing, reports `missingFileSupports` and supplies a fixer *only* when `autoFixTestTemplate` is not false; fixer calls `insertSupportsTemplate(...)`. - Never attempts to infer a real story path or IDs; it always uses a placeholder or user-supplied template string (REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE). - `normalizeReqId(raw)` and `normalizeReqPrefixInDescription(description)`: - Only operate when a recognizable `REQ...` token is present. - Normalize case to upper, convert underscores/spaces to hyphens, collapse repeated hyphens, and convert parenthesis/spacing variants into canonical `[REQ-XXX]` form. - Return `null` when there is no REQ-like token, so no fixer is produced in ambiguous cases (REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT, REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE, REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE). - `createUpdatedStringLiteralRaw(originalNode, newValue, sourceCode)` preserves original quoting and escapes only the literal content, not surrounding code or indentation (REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE). - `handleItOrTestCall` respects `autoFixTestPrefixFormat` and only offers a fixer when: - The description has a malformed-but-recognizable REQ prefix that `normalizeReqPrefixInDescription` can fix, and - The description is a literal, and - `autoFixTestPrefixFormat !== false`. - In the case of missing prefixes, it reports an error but provides **no** fix, aligning with REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE.
3) Tests for this story - File: tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts - File header includes: ```ts /** * @supports docs/stories/020.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION.story.md REQ-TEST-FILE-SUPPORTS REQ-TEST-FRAMEWORK-COMPAT REQ-TEST-PATTERN-DETECT * @supports docs/stories/021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX.story.md REQ-TEST-FIX-TEMPLATE REQ-TEST-FIX-PREFIX-FORMAT REQ-TEST-FIX-SAFE REQ-TEST-FIX-PRESERVE REQ-TEST-FIX-PLACEHOLDER REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE */ ``` - Under `require-test-traceability` invalid cases, tests explicitly cover: - Missing file-level `@supports`: - Input has no `@supports` comment and a valid `[REQ-ONE]` test name. - Expected autofix output shows the placeholder JSDoc `@supports` block inserted at the top with the TODO line, and the rest of the file unchanged. - Confirms file-level template insertion and preservation of existing tests (File-Level Template, Template Quality, Quality Standards). - No prefix present: - Input has `it('missing prefix', () => {});` with a valid `@supports` above. - Test expects a `missingReqPrefix` error but **no** autofix output, confirming that the rule does not invent `[REQ-...]` prefixes (REQ-TEST-FIX-NO-INFERENCE, Error Handling). - Malformed prefixes: - `[ REQ-TEST-FIX ]` → `[REQ-TEST-FIX]` (spacing fix). - `[REQ_TEST_FIX]` → `[REQ-TEST-FIX]` (underscore to hyphen). - `[req-lowercase]` → `[REQ-LOWERCASE]` (case normalization). - `(REQ-PAREN)` → `[REQ-PAREN]` (parentheses to brackets). - In each case, only the prefix formatting changes; test names and bodies remain otherwise identical (Format Fixes, Quality Standards, Error Handling). - Valid cases ensure: - A correctly-annotated file with a valid `[REQ-TRACE-123]` test name is left unchanged (no autofix), confirming non-intrusive behavior on compliant code.
4) Test execution - Ran the full test suite with verbose Jest output: - Command: `npm test -- --runInBand --verbose`. - Result: exit code 0. - Output includes: - `PASS tests/rules/require-test-traceability.test.ts` - Shows both valid and invalid cases for `require-test-traceability`, including cases for malformed prefixes and missing file-level `@supports` for Stories 020.0 and 021.0. - Overall Jest summary: - Test Suites: 39 passed, 39 total - Tests: 300 passed, 300 total - Confirms all tests validating this story’s behavior are present and passing.
5) Documentation - user-docs (API reference for `traceability/require-test-traceability`) documents: - That when running ESLint with `--fix`, the rule: - Inserts a file-level `@supports` placeholder template at the top of test files when missing, with a TODO line instructing developers to replace placeholders. - Normalizes malformed `[REQ-XXX]` prefixes (spacing, underscores, casing, parentheses) in test names without changing test semantics. - Documents configuration options: `autoFixTestTemplate`, `autoFixTestPrefixFormat`, and `testSupportsTemplate`, matching the story’s configuration section.
6) Acceptance criteria coverage - File-Level Template: Implemented via `ensureFileSupportsAnnotation` + `insertSupportsTemplate`; verified by RuleTester invalid case output and passing tests. - Format Fixes: Implemented via `normalizeReqId`/`normalizeReqPrefixInDescription` and the `handleItOrTestCall` fixer; tests cover the specific malformed examples from the story (spacing, `_` vs `-`, case, parentheses). - Template Quality: Template uses an explicit placeholder story path, placeholder REQ IDs, and a clear TODO instruction line; visible in helper implementation and tests. - Quality Standards: Only comments and string literals are modified; tests confirm no changes to test implementation code and that already-correct cases are untouched. - Integration: Implemented within the existing ESLint rule architecture with `meta.fixable: "code"`, and exercised via Jest RuleTester under the standard ESLint `--fix` semantics. - User Experience: Behavior is deterministic and consistent; placeholders and normalized prefixes match the documented examples. - Error Handling: Fixers are only offered when normalization is unambiguous; otherwise the rule reports errors without attempting risky fixes. - Documentation: API docs describe both the auto-fix behaviors and the configuration options, satisfying the documentation acceptance criterion.
traceability.notes: The story 021.0-DEV-TEST-ANNOTATION-AUTO-FIX is fully implemented. The `require-test-traceability` rule and its helpers provide safe, non-semantic auto-fixes for missing file-level `@supports` annotations (with clear placeholder templates) and for malformed `[REQ-XXX]` prefixes in test names. The behavior matches the story’s implementation notes, respects all safety and non-inference constraints, and is thoroughly covered by Jest RuleTester tests which are currently all passing. User-facing documentation also describes these auto-fix capabilities and configuration options. Therefore, all acceptance criteria and requirements for this story are satisfied.
